extracted.intended_audience: Indiana state and local government employees, records managers, county/local records custodians
extracted.subtask_description: Official guidance for managing, digitizing, retaining, transferring, and disposing of state and local government records in Indiana, including electronic records, imaging/microfilm standards, and use of the State Records Center and Archives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Records Center storage (inactive paper records)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Indiana State Records Center provides state government agencies with secure off-site storage for Inactive paper records: those records that have not yet reached their disposition date, and the agency still owns them, but they are no longer used frequently and do not need to be stored in the agency's office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only records that are 'inactive' (not frequently used, not yet reached disposition date, and still owned by the agency) are eligible for Records Center storage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records must be approved on retention schedule before transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The records must be approved for Records Center transfer on the records retention schedule that covers them, before Records Center staff can accept transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must verify that the appropriate records series on their retention schedule authorizes transfer to the Records Center prior to attempting to transfer records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records Center disposition services for scheduled destruction or transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Records Center also provides courtesy destruction services for records that have reached their disposition date and are scheduled for destruction, and will destroy or transfer records to the State Archives when they are stored in the Records Center and have reached their disposition date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If records stored in the Records Center reach their disposition date, the Center can either destroy them (if scheduled) or transfer them to the State Archives. Agencies should rely on the retention schedule for disposition instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records request and delivery services limited to agency use
rubrics_metrics.description: While your records are still living in storage out at the Records Center, their staff provides records request and delivery services, any time you need a file or even whole boxes returned to your office! Those services are only available to you, not to the public. Public record requests get fulfilled by the agency, never the Records Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the owning agency may request retrievals from the Records Center; public records requests must be handled by the agency itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaging and microfilm standards for permanent preservation (SIML)
rubrics_metrics.description: SIML specializes in creating high quality microfilm using standards prescribed by the Indiana Rules of Court, Administrative Rule 6 for permanent preservation, following these standards to ensure that documents filmed today will be accessible up to 500 years from now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Microfilming intended for permanent preservation must follow Administrative Rule 6; adherence to these standards is required to ensure very long-term accessibility (up to 500 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reformatting services (SIML)
rubrics_metrics.description: They also provide reformatting services for IARA and for government agencies, specializing in converting organizational records to any medium, to increase their accessibility and improve their preservation. Services include paper and microfilm to digital, paper and digital to microfilm, and processing and duplication of already-existing agency microfilm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIML will convert between paper, microfilm, and digital formats and can process/duplicate existing microfilm; agencies should consult SIML for reformatting projects to improve access and preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention defined by record series on retention schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: How long an agency must keep a record (retention) is laid out in a record series on the records retention schedule that applies to the agency or office. Each record series also contains information on where the records can be stored, the formats in which the record most frequently appears, and (of course) the type of information covered by that Record Series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must identify the applicable record series on their retention schedule to determine retention period, storage location, acceptable formats, and the information types covered by that series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of state agency retention schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: State Agency retention schedules include the General Retention Schedule for all State Agencies and a number of agency and division-specific schedules that varies by agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consult both the General Retention Schedule and any agency/division-specific schedules applicable to their records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of county/local retention schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: County/Local retention schedules include the County/Local General Retention Schedule and a number of office-specific schedules that are specific to each type of county/local office, rather than any individual government entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: County and local offices must use the County/Local General Retention Schedule plus the office-specific schedule appropriate to their office type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition options at end of retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: What happens at the end of a records scheduled retention period (disposition), is usually one of two things: it gets destroyed (by the agency or local office, or by the State Records Center for records stored there) OR it gets transferred to the State Archives (also by the agency/office or by the Records Center), to become part of the State's permanent research collection of records with historical value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disposition is determined by the retention schedule; agencies must either destroy records per schedule or transfer them to the Archives when instructed. The Archives accepts both paper and electronic records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition rules for electronic records
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike the Records Center, the State Archives collects electronic records as well as paper, so disposition instructions to transfer records to the Archives don't change if the agency switches to maintaining them in electronic format, only the method of transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disposition calls for transfer to the Archives, agencies must follow the same disposition instruction regardless of whether records are paper or electronic; logistics differ but the end disposition remains the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other disposition options for county/local records
rubrics_metrics.description: Other possible dispositions for County/Local records include maintaining permanent records right there in the office, or transferring records to a local historical society or archive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: County/local offices may retain permanent records in-office or transfer them to local repositories where appropriate; consult the County/Local Records Custodian Handbook for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: IARA Electronic Records Program standards and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: IARA's Electronic Records Program assists state and local government employees with the special challenges of organizing, digitizing, maintaining, destroying, and applying records retention requirements to electronic records. This includes guidelines for all electronic records, standards for digitized records and electronic records management systems, policy on destroying original records after digitization, and all the help with managing, retaining, and deleting email...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow IARA's guidelines for electronic records formats, digitization standards, ERMS requirements, and the policy governing whether originals may be destroyed after digitization; follow program resources and training for email management and other e-records topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendor qualifications for converting public records
rubrics_metrics.description: Vendor Qualifications for Converting Public Records (resource listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies using external vendors for conversion/reformatting should ensure vendors meet the qualifications outlined by IARA (see the Vendor Qualifications resource for specifics).
